supporting_observations.claim: The observed periodic HTTPS activity from 13:37 to 14:07 UTC is consistent with the approved PixelForge updater: pfupdater.exe was running and its connections through the proxy were to updates.pixelforge-suite.com, at roughly five-minute intervals. One attempt received a 407 authentication-required response.
pfupdater.exe started at 13:37:43 UTC and exited at 14:08:08 UTC, enclosing the sequence of periodic updater connections.

The domain controller recorded a successful NTLM network logon for sam.okafor on WS-SOKAFOR-01, originating from WS-LMARTINS-01. Given the supplied context that sam.okafor is the sole IT administrator and remote administration is only done from WS-SOKAFOR-01, this account use from the user workstation warrants investigation, but the records do not show what action followed.

FILE-NWD-01 made an inbound RPC connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 at 13:31 UTC. The supplied IT-practice context describes workstation patching as initiated from WS-SOKAFOR-01, but these records do not identify the RPC operation or show remote code execution.

DropboxUpdate.exe ran as SYSTEM on WS-LMARTINS-01. The inventory says Dropbox is not an approved file-sharing service. A DNS query for x7k9m2.akamaized.net occurred near that run, but the records attribute the query to svchost.exe and do not establish that DropboxUpdate.exe initiated it or connected to the resolved address.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT destinations, status, and tunnel byte counts, but not the HTTPS contents.
The DNS record for x7k9m2.akamaized.net attributes the query to svchost.exe; the available records do not identify the initiating application.
The FILE-NWD-01-to-workstation RPC connection has no accompanying record identifying its RPC method, authentication context, or resulting action.
The available records do not establish the process or action associated with the sam.okafor network logon on WS-SOKAFOR-01.
claims_not_established: That the periodic HTTPS connections were malicious; the observed sequence aligns with the approved PixelForge updater.
That DropboxUpdate.exe caused the unusual DNS query or made an external connection.
That the sam.okafor logon was used for unauthorized administration, or that it led to a successful privileged action.
That the RPC connection from FILE-NWD-01 resulted in remote execution, persistence, or compromise.
That data was exfiltrated or that WS-LMARTINS-01 was compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Review WS-SOKAFOR-01 authentication and process telemetry around 13:26 UTC to determine the purpose and outcome of the sam.okafor logon.
Collect FILE-NWD-01 and WS-LMARTINS-01 RPC, SMB, and process-creation telemetry around 13:31 UTC to identify the caller, operation, and any resulting execution.
Verify the DropboxUpdate.exe file hash, signature, installation source, service configuration, and whether Dropbox is present or used elsewhere in the environment.
Obtain detailed proxy, DNS, and endpoint network telemetry around 13:42 UTC to identify the initiator and determine whether any connection followed the x7k9m2.akamaized.net lookup.
Confirm with the user or software inventory owner whether Dropbox was intentionally installed on WS-LMARTINS-01.
